clue.text: Knight might ride on this barren area

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the mount a mounted knight sits on
second meaning: a miners' term for a mass of barren rock in a vein

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a mining term: a horse is a barren stretch of rock interrupting a mineral vein.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight's steed is the obvious mount, and miners use the same word for an unproductive mass of rock within a lode.

clue.text: Cushion punch after embraces

indicators.note: after says the piece named before it comes second, following the other

parts.note: to have is to hold or embrace
a sock is a hard blow

explanation.surface: A cushion is punched after a round of hugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the second piece behind the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a firm stuffed kneeling cushion, as used in church pews.

clue.text: Finally, transport cafe — roll on

indicators.note: transport means carry elsewhere, so the letters are moved into new places

parts.note: the letters of cafe, roll and on

explanation.surface: At last a lorry drivers' cafe is in sight: keep going!
explanation.walkthrough: A transport cafe is a British roadside diner for lorry drivers, so 'transport' hides in a familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Once for all means finally, definitively, never to be repeated.

clue.text: Outmoded field of study concerning French soul

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ame is French for soul

explanation.surface: An obsolete academic discipline about the French spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Reame is an obsolete spelling of realm, and a realm can be a sphere or field of knowledge.

clue.text: Vagrant, true one in transit

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders, so the letters stray out of their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A genuine tramp who is travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: En route is the French borrowing for on the way, travelling between places.

clue.text: Yankee caravan? One jeering behind it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American word for a towed caravan or mobile home
second meaning: from the old verb trail, to quiz or make fun of, so one who mocks; and it trails behind

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives trail as an old colloquial verb meaning to tease or make fun of, so one who does it is a jeerer; 'behind it' adds that a towed van follows the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a towed caravan a trailer, and the noun from trail in its teasing sense names a mocker.

clue.text: Renovating three-piece could make this dwelling rich

indicators.note: renovating means remaking, so the letters are rebuilt in another order
the answer plus a further word would make the rearranged phrase, so that word is taken away

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, the letters set aside

explanation.surface: Doing up a three-piece suite would make this home luxurious.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer together with the word rich would give the letters of three-piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A teepee is a conical tent home of the Plains peoples of North America.

clue.text: Location finder is bidirectional and excellent on most craft

indicators.note: most of something means all but its last letter
bidirectional means it works both ways, reading the same forwards and back

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent
an ark is a craft, cut short

explanation.surface: A navigational device that works both ways and is great on most boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bidirectional' is a straight hint as well as an indicator: the answer is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar detects objects by reflected radio waves, so it finds their position.

clue.text: Hellebore fascinating woman — pip is lost with being dropped

indicators.note: being dropped means left out, so that word's letter is removed

parts.note: a witch is a bewitching, fascinating woman
the pip is a fit of illness; weed is Scots for a sudden feverish attack
W is the abbreviation for with, here removed

explanation.surface: A charming woman loses heart when a fruit seed is discarded from the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces make WITCH and WEED; the W standing for 'with' is then dropped. The parse of 'is lost' is uncertain and is treated here as joining.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchweed is a name for the American white or false hellebore, a poisonous plant.

clue.text: Worm is two times circled by old hound disregarding master

indicators.note: circled by says one piece is ringed by another
disregarding means ignoring, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a lyam or lyme was an old word for a leashed hound
M for master, removed
T for time, twice

explanation.surface: A worm is twice ringed by an old dog with no owner.
explanation.definitionFit: The lytta is a worm-shaped cartilage under a dog's tongue, which old lore took for a worm.

clue.text: Free to include edition that's worked up again

indicators.note: to include means to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to rid is to free
ed is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: A free copy is included in a reworked new release.
explanation.definitionFit: Redid is the past tense of redo, to work up or do over again.

clue.text: Nine-pillared building neatly seen

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the following words are put together afresh in a new order

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A building with nine pillars that looks tidy from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nine-pillared building' looks like the whole definition, but the definition stops at the adjective; 'building' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Enneastyle is the architectural adjective for a portico with nine columns, from Greek ennea, nine.

clue.text: Secretary's first to mind about King's presumed misprint

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the initial letter of Secretary

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to mind is to care
R for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A secretary first takes note of a supposed typing error in the king's letter.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARRE is a word in Shakespeare's All's Well that Ends Well that editors take to be a printer's error.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries list scarre as a Shakespearean word of unknown meaning, generally assumed to be a corruption in the printed text.

clue.text: Such as a group of maids a-milking joining only child, little 'un

definitions.text: Such as a group of maids a-milking

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words
a tad is a small child

explanation.surface: Eight milkmaids from the carol, joined by a lone small child.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Twelve Days of Christmas the true love gives eight maids a-milking, so they form a set of eight.
explanation.definitionFit: An octad is any set of eight, as the eight milkmaids of the carol's eighth day are.

clue.text: Up-to-date ingenuity replacing ads in store

indicators.note: replacing means putting in different places, so the letters change position

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Modern cleverness swaps the advertisements in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness is skill and cleverness, a synonym of ingenuity; 'up-to-date' adds the sense of being quick and current.

clue.text: Ludicrous poem is about Loch's lustreless gem

indicators.note: something ludicrous is absurd and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a, short for about (circa)
L is the map abbreviation for loch

explanation.surface: A silly poem praises a dull jewel found by a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Semi-opal is a variety of opal lacking the play of colour, so a gem without lustre.

clue.text: Being peevish in speech I squint

parts.note: cross means irritable

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so a word stands in for one that sounds the same

parts.note: the pronoun spoken is the same as the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Speaking crossly, I peer narrowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I squint' looks like the definition, but the I is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-eye is a squint in which the eyes turn inward toward the nose.

clue.text: Desert conflict contained by anarchist

indicators.note: contained by says the first piece sits inside the next one

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary leftist
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: A war in the desert waged by a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' reads as sand, but it is the noun stressed on the second syllable, as in 'just deserts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert in this sense is what one deserves, a recompense or reward.

clue.text: Cue story about chivalry

indicators.note: about can mean turned around in all directions, so the letters are moved

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A prompt for a tale about knightly conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalry is gallant politeness, and courtesy is a synonym for such good manners.

clue.text: Cart rolling up during morning run is early drinker's datum?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rolling up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dray is a brewer's cart

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece goes inside the next

parts.note: am, before noon
R for run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A brewer's cart rolls in after a morning jog, to suit the early drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The joking rule is that it is acceptable to drink once 'the sun is over the yardarm', so the yardarm is the drinker's reference point.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is the end of a ship's yard; the saying makes it a reference line for when drinking may start.

clue.text: Whirling tender god?

indicators.note: something whirling turns round, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: tender means painful, sore

explanation.surface: A spinning, affectionate deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender god' suggests a loving deity, which Eros is, but 'tender' is the word that gets turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love.

clue.text: "Without date" classically put on temple's interior monuments

parts.note: s.a., Latin sine anno, without date
the cella is the inner chamber of a classical temple

explanation.surface: Undated classical monuments placed inside a temple.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacella, plural of sacellum, are small chapels or monuments within a church.

clue.text: In a rarely used way preposterously do West African

indicators.text: In a rarely used way preposterously
indicators.note: preposterous in its old literal sense means having the hinder part first, so the last letter goes to the front

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, to rook

explanation.surface: Do something absurdly in an unusual manner, says a man from West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Preposterous comes from Latin prae (before) and posterus (after): the back comes first. That rare literal sense moves the final letter to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kroo are a people of the Liberian coast, famed as seamen; the word names a member of that people.

clue.text: Diverting a niece with an Oxonian celebration

indicators.note: diverting means turning aside, sending the letters off in other directions

parts.note: the letters of a, niece and an, with 'with' joining them

explanation.surface: Entertaining a niece at a university festivity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Encaenia is Oxford University's annual commemoration ceremony, where honorary degrees are conferred.

clue.text: Blubber about that woman's new ball

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: to blubber is to cry
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone sobs about a woman's ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the cherry is slang for a new red ball, from its shiny colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers call a fresh, shiny red ball the cherry.

clue.text: Eg, Fred Baron — chap who adds value

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for baron
a valuable person is an asset

explanation.surface: Fred the baron is a valuable chap to have around.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Basset is a long-running British newspaper cartoon dog, a basset hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon hound Fred is a basset, a short-legged breed of hunting dog, so he is an example.

clue.text: Rising celestial body with good height makes a halo

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: an orb is a heavenly sphere
G for good
H for height

explanation.surface: A star climbing high in good weather forms a ring of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Brogh is a Scots variant of brough, a halo or ring round the sun or moon.

clue.text: According to art chaps will be identical in Scotland

parts.note: s.a., Latin secundum artem, according to art
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Artistic men will look alike north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is the pharmacists' abbreviation for secundum artem, according to the rules of the art.
explanation.definitionFit: Samen is an old Scots form of same, meaning identical.

clue.text: Delight as little Italian embraces eccentricity

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant
e is the symbol for eccentricity in geometry

explanation.surface: A small Italian person's oddness is a joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little Italian' suggests a person, but it is an eatery cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is a source of delight or pleasure.

clue.text: King replacing line tips cases for northerners

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: K for king
L for line, the letter swapped out
to list is to tip or lean over

explanation.surface: A monarch swaps a queue for advice in Scottish crates.
explanation.definitionFit: Kist is the Scots and northern English word for a chest or box.

clue.text: Freak freed in a prank played by French

indicators.note: freak as a verb means to go wild or be thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball let loose in a practical joke by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freak' looks like the definition, a whim or prank, but it is the signal; the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Fredaine is a French word for an escapade or youthful folly, borrowed into English.

clue.text: With moving welcome we will take off old Native American

indicators.note: moving letters around changes their order
taking off means removing, so those letters are subtracted

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A heartfelt greeting for an ancient American visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olmec were an ancient civilisation of the Mexican Gulf coast, predating the Maya.

clue.text: Act central to Whisky Galore! managed by Scots personality

definitions.note: a verb defined by the act it performs

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
sel is Scots for self

explanation.surface: The key scene of the Scottish whisky comedy was handled by a local character.
explanation.walkthrough: Whisky Galore! is a comedy of Hebridean islanders hiding salvaged whisky from searching excisemen; ransel is Scots for to search, especially for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The film turns on customs men hunting for hidden bottles, and ransel is the Scots verb for searching houses for stolen goods.

clue.text: Notorious mimic's dull and standard blah

parts.note: grey means dull, dreary
par is the standard or norm
blah and rot both mean nonsense

explanation.surface: A famous impressionist's act is dull, ordinary nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: The African grey parrot is renowned as the best talking bird, a famous imitator of speech.

clue.text: Keen pen displays integrity without prejudice

parts.note: to keen is to wail; hone is a dialect verb to moan or pine
a sty is a pig pen

explanation.surface: A sharp writer shows fair-minded principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen pen' reads as a sharp writer, but keen is the verb to lament, and pen an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty is uprightness and fairness, integrity exercised without bias.

clue.text: First schoolgirl finding service in Rome

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
A is first, top grade

explanation.surface: The top girl in the school finds a church service while in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rome' marks a Latin word, not a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Missa is Latin for the Mass, the eucharistic service of the Roman church.
